elements.requirement: A non-molestation order is an order containing provision prohibiting the respondent from molesting an associated person, prohibiting the respondent from molesting a relevant child, or containing both provisions.
elements.quote: an order containing either or both of the following provisions— (a) provision prohibiting a person ( “the respondent”) from molesting another person who is associated with the respondent; (b) provision prohibiting the respondent from molesting a relevant child

elements.requirement: The court may make a non-molestation order upon an application made by a person associated with the respondent, whether that application is made in other family proceedings or without any other family proceedings being instituted.
elements.quote: if an application for the order has been made (whether in other family proceedings or without any other family proceedings being instituted) by a person who is associated with the respondent

elements.requirement: The court may make a non-molestation order in any family proceedings to which the respondent is a party if it considers the order should be made for the benefit of any other party to the proceedings or any relevant child, even if no application has been made.
elements.quote: if in any family proceedings to which the respondent is a party the court considers that the order should be made for the benefit of any other party to the proceedings or any relevant child even though no such application has been made

elements.requirement: For the purposes of making a non-molestation order, family proceedings include proceedings in which the court has made an emergency protection order under section 44 of the Children Act 1989 containing an exclusion requirement as defined in section 44A(3) of that Act.
elements.quote: “family proceedings” includes proceedings in which the court has made an emergency protection order under section 44 of the Children Act 1989 which includes an exclusion requirement (as defined in section 44A(3) of that Act)

elements.requirement: Where an agreement to marry is terminated, an applicant may not apply for a non-molestation order by virtue of section 62(3)(e) after the end of the period of three years beginning with the day on which the agreement is terminated.
elements.quote: no application under subsection (2)(a) may be made by virtue of section 62(3)(e) by reference to that agreement after the end of the period of three years beginning with the day on which it is terminated

elements.requirement: A court considering whether to make an occupation order must also consider whether to exercise the power to make a non-molestation order on its own motion.
elements.quote: A court considering whether to make an occupation order shall also consider whether to exercise the power conferred by subsection (2)(b)

elements.requirement: Where the context permits, the term applicant in relation to a non-molestation order includes the person for whose benefit such an order is or would be made under the court's own-motion powers.
elements.quote: “the applicant”, in relation to a non-molestation order, includes (where the context permits) the person for whose benefit such an order would be or is made in exercise of the power conferred by subsection (2)(b)

elements.requirement: If a civil partnership agreement is terminated, no application under section 42 may be made by virtue of section 62(3)(eza) by reference to that agreement after the end of the period of three years beginning with the day on which it is terminated.
elements.quote: no application under this section may be made by virtue of section 62(3)(eza) by reference to that agreement after the end of the period of three years beginning with the day on which it is terminated

elements.requirement: In deciding whether and how to exercise its powers under section 42, the court must have regard to all the circumstances, including the need to secure the health, safety, and well-being of the applicant and of any relevant child.
elements.quote: the court shall have regard to all the circumstances including the need to secure the health, safety and well-being— (a) of the applicant ; and (b) of any relevant child

elements.requirement: A non-molestation order may refer to molestation in general, to particular acts of molestation, or to both.
elements.quote: A non-molestation order may be expressed so as to refer to molestation in general, to particular acts of molestation, or to both

elements.requirement: The court may make a non-molestation order for a specified period or until further order.
elements.quote: A non-molestation order may be made for a specified period or until further order

elements.requirement: A non-molestation order made in other family proceedings ceases to have effect if those underlying proceedings are withdrawn or dismissed.
elements.quote: A non-molestation order which is made in other family proceedings ceases to have effect if those proceedings are withdrawn or dismissed
